title: Deliver the product as a Manifest V3 Chrome extension with a content script, service worker, and extension-owned stylesheet
decision: Build the product as a Chrome extension on Manifest V3, written in TypeScript, with no UI framework: a content script performs DOM traversal and selector-based extraction of the question and answer option text from the active tab, a service worker coordinates activation and AI requests, and highlighting is applied by injecting a single generated CSS class onto matched answer elements using an extension-owned stylesheet scoped to that class name (no inline text, labels, or overlays). Diagnostic log entries are persisted in chrome.storage.local and surfaced through the Chrome extensions page. The AI provider integration, AI response parsing, and test harness remain unresolved research slots and are not selected here.
rationale: The SRS fixes the delivery surface: the product must be installable and operable as a Chrome extension inside the student's browser, triggered from the browser's extension controls while the quiz page stays open, and must operate on the page as displayed without a separate application or window (R-9). It must read the question and answer options from the displayed page itself with no student-supplied content (R-4), and it must apply a visual indication by styling only, adding no text, label, or other content to the page (R-11). A Manifest V3 extension with a content script is the only option that satisfies all three at once: the content script is the browser-sanctioned mechanism for reading and styling the live page in the active tab, and the service worker keeps request orchestration out of the page context. Styling via a single generated class in an extension-owned stylesheet is chosen over inline style attributes or injected elements because it is the smallest possible page mutation, which directly serves the quiet-failure and non-intrusiveness requirements (R-5, R-6, R-8) and the founder's decided position that the extension should do nothing when the page content is not what it expected. chrome.storage.local is chosen for logs because it persists across page close and reopen (R-7) while keeping log content off the quiz page entirely (R-7, R-8). TypeScript and the absence of a UI framework follow from the fact that no UI is ever rendered: there is no view layer to justify a framework, and typed parsing of model responses reduces the risk of a runtime fault surfacing visibly. This is a greenfield system with no recorded baseline, so no departure is being authorized and no migration evidence applies.

options_considered.option: A standalone web application or desktop application where the student pastes or uploads the question
options_considered.reason: Rejected: it violates R-4 (content must come from the displayed page with no student-supplied input) and R-9 (no separate application or window), and it forces the student to leave the quiz page.

options_considered.option: A browser userscript or bookmarklet injected into the page
options_considered.reason: Rejected: it is not installable through the browser's own extension installation mechanism nor triggerable from the browser's extension controls as R-9 requires, and it offers no persistent extension-local store for the diagnostic logs R-7 requires.

options_considered.option: A Chrome extension that renders its answers in a popup, side panel, or injected overlay element
options_considered.reason: Rejected: R-11 permits styling only and forbids adding text, label, or other content to the page, and R-3/R-2 require the indication on the quiz page itself with no additional window, panel, or overlay.

options_considered.option: A Chrome extension that applies highlighting via inline style attributes written directly onto answer elements
options_considered.reason: Rejected in favor of a single generated class in an extension-owned stylesheet: inline attributes scatter mutations across many elements and are harder to keep reversible and silent, which works against R-5, R-6, and R-8.

options_considered.option: A Chrome extension with a UI framework for its extension pages
options_considered.reason: Rejected: the product renders no UI at all, so a framework adds build and runtime surface without serving any requirement, and any framework error path is a visible-failure risk under R-8.
